translation: The most important event for me in the winter of 1993 was my father's return, which happened just a week before my mother got married.
One afternoon in December, he came to the school to find me.
I ran all the way to the main gate and through the iron bars, I saw him standing outside smoking from a distance.
Dressed in a long black trench coat, with the collar raised to cover half his face.
For some reason, even though I didn't get a clear look at him, I had the impression that he was having a tough time.
My heart ached and tears began to fall.
I never thought that my mother would consider remarrying.
Perhaps subconsciously, I felt that she should continue suffering because of my father's departure, just like me.
Besides, I feel she lacks the ability to find happiness.
Perhaps the truth is indeed so, but happiness has the ability to find her.
Isn't it true that as a beauty, she really doesn't have to work so hard?
She doesn't need to do anything.
Just standing in place is enough.
I still remember, the winter of that year was particularly long.
Halfway through April, the spring flowers had not yet blossomed.
The divorce of your parents has made you very depressed.
We hadn't had any new games for a long time, so we just sat aimlessly on the roof of the death tower every evening.
Among the body parts scattered in the yard, a few more arms were added.
We used hooks to gather them together, arranging them into a Thousand-Hand Guanyin.
In truth, my father knew nothing about doing business;
he only went to pay homage to a distant cousin who was not well-acquainted with us.
My grandmother had a sister who went to Beijing at an early age and later got married and had children there.
This cousin was the eldest son in her family, and within the entire family unit, he was always regarded as an odd one out.
You just said that everyone has a time when their luck begins, as if life suddenly gets reined in.
I should have been eight years old.
That autumn, my father left Jinan and went to Beijing alone.
Since then, I have been homeless.
I have no plans to keep the appointment.
Regardless of the reason, I believe there's no need for us to meet again.
I was sitting on the sofa, smoking one cigarette after another.
As it got darker and darker, there was a sudden knock at the door.
Deliver
The boy from the water station stood in the doorway, carrying a water bucket, saying that he was delivering water to a household in the western suburbs.
He wore a dirty, grey, woolen hat, his expression bewildered.
Our conversation was very difficult.
Every time I fall silent, I feel a pressure on my heart and just want to end this meeting quickly.
You seem to have noticed something, but you're still trying to find a topic of conversation.
The tea had cooled, the white mist in the room had dissipated, and you finally got up to leave.
Just as I closed the door and let out a sigh of relief, the doorbell rang again.
You were standing at the door, asking me to come to the small white building later.
Before I had the chance to refuse, you had already left the building.
I walked to the kitchen and turned off the stove.
Half of the water in the pot had evaporated, filling the whole room with white mist.
You sit down restlessly, watching me pour the tea.
"Do you still live with your grandmother and aunt?"
You ask.
I'll tell you, my grandmother has passed away, and now I live with my aunt.
"She never settled down," you ask.
"Mm-hmm.

The white breath you exhale, your hair, tousled by the wind, the slight trembling of your knees beneath the hem of your coat these things convince me that you truly exist before me and are not a continuation from a previous dream.
It's been eighteen years, it's no surprise if you don't recognize me.
You're not wearing any makeup, and your pale face is slightly swollen, but you have met everyone's expectations in the end, turning out to be a beauty.
Her peach-shaped face was gloomy, revealing an expression that suggested she had spent a long time in the big city.
You ask me if you look different from what I had imagined.
I gave a noncommittal smile.
To be honest, I've never imagined what you'd look like when you grow up.
For me, everything related to you has already been packed into file folders and sealed with wax.
It may hurt to say this, but honestly, I have no expectation of seeing you again.
I open my eyes.
You stand at the door.
I don't know how long you've been standing there, maybe you even saw me laughing in my dream.
And the sadness of waking up, at its weakest moment.
Cheng Gong, you whisper my name, your voice is very hoarse, it seems that you haven't spoken for a long time.
It's about to snow, the sky is terribly overcast, and it's pitch black inside the house.
The water on the stove was boiling, churning and bubbling.
I looked at you carefully for a moment, certain that I did not recognize you.
But in the dim light, I suddenly felt that this stranger standing opposite me seemed to have a deep connection with my life.
That feeling sends chills down your spine.
I tried hard to recall, memory cards flipping rapidly in my mind.
And then you said, "You are Li Jiaqi.
